summary: Tesla (TSLA, NASDAQ Global Select) is an electric vehicle, energy storage and autonomy company. This Valuatum equity research report dated 23 July 2026 rates the stock SELL with a 12-month target price of USD 333.20 versus a current price of USD 377.79, implying roughly -11.8% downside.
The core issue is a large optionality premium: Tesla's enterprise value allocates a majority of value to Autonomy and AI/Robotics despite no disclosed revenue in those pools.
The report concludes that the valuation requires aggressive margin expansion, core hardware profitability far above the current run-rate, and successful monetisation of autonomy and robotics options.

thesis.title: Massive Optionality Premium Exposure
thesis.text: Tesla's enterprise value allocates 56% to Autonomy and AI/Robotics despite zero disclosed revenue in either segment, leaving valuation highly exposed if those bets stall.

thesis.title: Aggressive Margin Expansion Bridge Required
thesis.text: Group EBIT margin must expand from 5.6% in 2026E to 11.8% by 2028E, requiring auto margin recovery and energy scale-up.

thesis.title: Core Hardware Profitability Mismatch
thesis.text: Automotive Core needs roughly USD 22 billion of EBIT on 5.5 million units to support its EV allocation, while 2025 segment EBIT was far lower.

thesisBreaker: If auto EBIT margin remains stuck below 6% while unsupervised FSD approval stalls beyond 24 months, the optionality premium collapses toward the bear case.

profile: Tesla designs, manufactures and sells battery electric vehicles, related software and automotive services, alongside a growing energy generation and storage business. The company is pursuing a strategic shift toward autonomous driving, Robotaxi ride-hailing and humanoid robotics, which investors increasingly view as central to its long-term value proposition.
